purpose: The documentation chrome, composed once in the app: a sticky header (at the inline start the compact menu button, the Azion Docs mark and the section links; an empty `AppHeader.Center` spacer; at the inline end `SearchTrigger` and then the app's actions, the way most docs sites end their header with the search), the navigation rail (`Sidebar` + `SidebarMenu`) on the inline start, resizable by dragging its edge and collapsible to a thin edge that brings it back, the article in the layout's `<main>`, the "On this page" rail (`DocTableOfContents`) on the inline end with its own slot below it — filled from the page itself: every `DocHeading` of level 2 or 3 that carries an `anchor`, and every `DocChangelogEntry`, rendered anywhere in the default slot registers with the layout, and the rail lists them in document order, so a page composed once in the app needs no wiring to feed its outline — and the footer under the article. The **document** scrolls: the header and both rails are sticky, so a full-page capture shows the whole article, the browser's find and scroll restoration work, and the dark canvas is painted to the end. The outline follows the reading position, a jump clears the sticky header, and below `lg` the rail moves into a drawer opened from the header. The `Command` palette lists every navigation page. Doc pages are only their article (page bodies with no header, rail or footer of their own), rendered through the default slot.
useWhen: Every documentation page (guide, reference, legal, changelog): put one `DocLayout` in the app's root (around `RouterView`) and render each page's article as its default slot.
A docs site that needs the navigation rail, the outline and the search palette without hand-composing `AppHeader`, `Sidebar`, `SidebarMenu`, `DocTableOfContents`, `Drawer` and `Command`.
avoidWhen: Never as part of a page: a page body is only its article, so it never renders `DocLayout`. A docs home with no outline rail is still a page inside the one layout: its headings carry no `anchor`, so nothing registers and the end rail is not rendered.
related: `DocTableOfContents` — the outline rail; the registered headings and `outlineGroups` are bound onto it.
`DocHeading` — headings whose anchor links the layout scrolls to, clearing the sticky header; an anchored level 2 or 3 heading registers itself as an outline entry.
`DocChangelogEntry` — each entry registers itself as a level 2 outline entry.
`useHeadingOutline` (`@aziontech/ui/use-heading-navigation`) — the registration a custom heading calls to join the outline.
`DocPageHeader`, `DocProse`, `DocPagination` — the article parts rendered in the default slot.
`Sidebar`, `SidebarMenu` — the navigation rail; `navigation` is mapped onto `SidebarMenu` groups.
`SearchTrigger`, `Command` — the header search and the palette it opens.
`shell/shell-docs` — the block that shows this layout with a sample docs tree.
bestPractices: Compose the layout once, in the app's root; each route renders only its article. Never put a header, a rail or an inner scroll area in a page.
Give every navigation row an `id` and an `href` (an in-app path is followed with the router; never `to`); leave `activeId` empty so the current page follows the route.

Never hand the outline to the layout: give each section heading a `DocHeading` with an `anchor` and the layout lists it, in document order, with the heading's own text, and tracks which one is in view. A heading without `anchor` stays out of the outline.

Put the theme switch in `navigation-footer`, the GitHub and Console links in `actions`, a call to action (`DocCallToAction`) in `aside`, and the site footer (`Footer variant="content"`) in `footer`. The `aside` content shows only on pages with an outline, so a shared call to action never lands on the docs home.
The page renders no `<main>` and no `ScrollArea` around the article: the document scrolls.

Bind `v-model:navigation-open` and `v-model:navigation-width` to state the app persists (local storage, a cookie) so the rail keeps the reader's size and collapsed state across pages and reloads; leave them unbound and the rail resets on each mount.

A drill row (`type: 'drill'`) opens its level in place; the rail's Back then reads `Back to Docs` at the first level. Set `rootLabel` when the tree is not the whole docs (`Back to API reference`); never add a hand-made Back row to `navigation`.
